statement: Cheaper memory use per inference in newer models could lower the hardware cost of serving tokens, weakening the link between token volume growth and accelerator and memory purchases.
why: Token economics decide how much hardware each unit of inference demand actually requires, so efficiency jumps can break the usual demand read-through.

impact.mechanism: Lower memory per served token cuts hardware needed per token, though cheaper inference can also raise total usage and offset the saving.

evidence.excerpt: DeepSeek's new model could stoke concerns about a slowdown

reasoning: The document reports only a share-price reaction and an analyst's concern, with no efficiency figure; the effect on hardware demand per token is therefore inferred and could be offset by higher usage.

confidence.basis: Inference from qualitative analyst commentary in one secondary outlet, with no efficiency figure stated in the document.

dispersion: The same analyst notes upcoming models from Meta and OpenAI may have greater industry impact.
